channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Nigeria bets on digital payments to rewire global finance
item.description: Nigeria is doubling down on digital innovation to fix what it calls a broken global payment system, one that keeps developing economies on the margins of trade and finance.

item.title: Airtel Africa eyes Starlink deal to power next-gen connectivity across 14 African markets
item.description: Airtel Africa is in advanced talks with SpaceX to integrate Starlink’s direct-to-cell satellite technology into its network, a potential game-changer for rural connectivity across fourteen African countries, including Kenya.

item.title: Africa’s wealthiest billionaire commits $1 million to a scholarship fund for business graduates
item.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, has committed $1.1 million, to fund postgraduate business education in Nigeria, reinforcing a growing trend of billionaire-backed human capital investment across the continent.

item.title: Western energy traders win Libya oil supply deals in strategic shift away from Russia
item.description: Libya has awarded key fuel supply tenders to major Western energy traders, marking a significant shift away from Russian refined product imports as the North African producer restructures its oil sector.

item.title: Egypt to roll out largest ever Mediterranean gas drilling project as Western investors gear up
item.description: Egypt is preparing to roll out its largest-ever Mediterranean gas drilling campaign in 2026, in a move officials say will strengthen domestic supply and reduce reliance on imports.

item.title: South African gold miner becomes first major casualty of Ghana’s tighter resource control
item.description: South Africa’s Gold Fields will formally relinquish ownership and operatorship of the Damang mine on April 18, 2026, marking a significant turning point in Ghana’s evolving strategy to increase national control over its mineral wealth.

item.title: Morocco targets gold and copper investors with 13,000 sq km mining exploration
item.description: Morocco has launched a sweeping new mining tender covering 13,000 square kilometres, signalling a stronger push to attract global investment into its mineral sector.

item.title: Risevest secures SEC licence after regulatory hurdles
item.description: After months of regulatory back-and-forth, Nigerian fintech startup Risevest has finally secured a Fund and Portfolio Manager licence from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) a move that brings its investment operations under official oversight and ends a long spell of uncertainty.

item.title: Rwanda’s new mining blocks draw 73 investor bids
item.description: Rwanda’s mining industry is seeing renewed investor interest as the government reports receiving at least 73 applications for 10 mining blocks unveiled in mid-2025. According to the Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board, the blocks have already attracted strong competition, leading to successful awards for areas including Nduba, Rweru-Kimvubu, Juru, Mamfu-Rwasama, Remera, Rugarama and Rweru.

item.title: Egypt eyes $590 million European loan to advance Alexandria Metro expansion
item.description: Egypt is pursuing a €500 million ($590 million) loan from European financial institutions to support the second phase of the Alexandria Metro project, according to a report by Asharq Business.
